source.title: Understanding Multimodal Hallucination with Parameter-Free Representation Alignment
source.authors: Yue-Qian Wang; Jian-Xin Liang; Yuxuan Wang; Hui-Shuai Zhang; Dong-Yan Zhao

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis but does not test whether independently trained models become more similar to one another with scale. It measures alignment of MLLM image representations to object annotations or image descriptions, and relates that to object hallucination.
record.gate_note: Pfram results concern model-to-annotation or model-to-description alignment, not convergence between model representations. The paper also reports no paired vision-model/language-model alignment test. Its results on hallucination and Pfram are recorded under fits_no_version; no result tests V1–V7.
record.test_reason: Pfram compares MLLM and ViT image representations with human object annotations, or with MPNet embeddings of GPT-4o captions, and correlates this with POPE hallucination accuracy. No result compares independently trained models with each other as scale or capability grows. The Huh et al. mutual k-NN metric is borrowed as a tool, not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that Pfram alignment with object annotations correlates strongly and consistently with object hallucination across MLLMs. LLM size, projector type and alignment with brief descriptions do not correlate strongly. They also use Pfram to diagnose modules, instructions and alternative ViTs.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes Pfram to measure representation-system alignment with annotations; it does not apply the original studies' inter-model convergence tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports Pfram measurements across different similarity metrics, k settings, datasets, and representation targets. These vary the annotation-alignment measurement, not a model-to-model convergence test.

fits_no_version.finding: MLLM image-representation alignment with object annotations correlates with POPE accuracy (r≈0.65–0.78, p≤0.04) at k=100. Most other k and summary settings on OIv7 are also significant; AMBER is mostly non-significant at k other than 100 (e.g. k=200 input kNN is significant).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment of MLLM image representations to object annotations tracks object-hallucination accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Alignment of MLLM image representations to MPNet embeddings of GPT-4o captions does not correlate significantly with POPE accuracy (r≈0.13–0.53, all p>0.05). Resampler-projector MLLMs show higher caption alignment than linear-projector ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neighbourhood alignment between MLLM image representations and a text encoder's caption embeddings does not track object-hallucination accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Within a ViT pre-training objective, larger models generally align better with object annotations (SAM excepted). The objective matters more than size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Visual encoder size and objective affect alignment with human object annotations.

record.problems: The evidence is not a test of inter-model convergence: Pfram compares model representations to annotations or descriptions. The MLLM correlation analysis covers 10 models and two datasets; the ViT size comparisons are shown in a figure rather than tabulated.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-model Pfram values for all additional k settings and representation summaries in Tables 3–10 are omitted because they concern model-to-annotation/description alignment and are not separate tests of any listed convergence version.

untested.parts: Model-to-model alignment across architectures or objectives as scale grows. ViT size effects are measured only against annotations.
Alignment of independent vision and language models on paired data as both improve. The Gdes alignment keeps the text model fixed and uses POPE accuracy rather than capability.
Recurring features or circuits across models.
Metric, k and data dependence of model-to-model convergence. k and metric are varied, but only for annotation alignment.
Incompleteness or plateau of inter-model alignment, and its causes.

record.verdict_notes: The closest point to V2 is the Gdes condition. It uses mutual k-NN between MLLM image representations and caption embeddings from a fixed text encoder, but it is not framed as, nor designed as, a convergence test. Researchers may wish to note its null correlation with hallucination accuracy as weak indirect evidence only. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Whether independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data become more aligned as scale and capability increase.
Alignment between vision and language model representations of paired images and captions as both models improve.
Convergence across random seeds of the same architecture, including shared features or subspaces.
Whether representations can be mapped, stitched, compared by relative representations, or aligned without paired data.
Whether interpretable features or circuits recur across models.

Whether measured convergence between models depends on metric settings and input data. Pfram settings vary, but the study measures model-to-annotation or model-to-description alignment rather than model-to-model convergence.
Whether inter-model alignment is incomplete or plateaus, or is explained by shared training data or objectives.

rows.note: The correlation is across the ten MLLMs; it measures alignment to descriptions versus hallucination accuracy, not model-to-model alignment.
rows.check: Link to none is acceptable. Gdes is a fixed language model's (MPNet) embedding of GPT-4o captions, so this is image-vs-text alignment. But the text side is fixed, the image side sits inside MLLMs trained on caption data, and POPE accuracy is a hallucination score, not a general capability measure. The weak, non-significant r (0.26–0.37, p≥0.30) does not cleanly test V2. Same applies to r6–r8.
